section_summary: The opening documents concern reports that Australia offered wheat and flour to Japan and Japanese-controlled markets on extended credit, and the State Department’s inquiry into those reports. A separate exchange asks whether Japanese government bonds intended for sale in the Philippine Islands fall under the Securities Act of 1933. The section then reproduces the Act, which continues beyond page 36.

people.name: Keith Officer
people.role: Australian counselor of the British Embassy

people.name: McDermott
people.role: official who spoke with the press

people.name: Jerome N. Frank
people.role: Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission

subfiles.title: Letter concerning Australian wheat and flour credits
subfiles.about: Reports Australian wheat and flour offers to Japan and asks that credit sales be discouraged.
subfiles.summary: Mallon reports extended credit on Australian sales to Japan and urges action through wheat trade or diplomatic channels.

subfiles.title: Proposal to consult the Australian counselor
subfiles.about: Recommends giving Keith Officer an aide-mémoire and explaining U.S. policy on credits to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Proposes an inquiry through the Australian counselor.

subfiles.title: Telephone report from the Department of Agriculture
subfiles.about: Records Agriculture’s handling of Mallon’s information and its suggestion of diplomatic action.
subfiles.summary: Agriculture passed Mallon’s report to the Wheat Committee and suggested State consider diplomatic channels.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Christy about Australian flour trade
subfiles.about: Explains Australia’s wartime control of the flour trade and Christy’s preference for diplomatic action.
subfiles.summary: Christy doubted the Wheat Committee could help and advised awaiting an Agriculture Department letter.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Australian wheat and flour sales
subfiles.about: Requests information on reported Australian wheat and flour sales on open credit.
subfiles.summary: Seeks confirmation of credit terms and low-priced flour offers.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Mallon’s report
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Mallon’s letter on Australian credits for wheat and flour purchases.
subfiles.summary: States that the matter is under study and promises further communication if warranted.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Keith Officer
subfiles.about: Records discussion of Australian credit sales and the Yunnan Railway.
subfiles.summary: Officer agreed to seek information from his government and emphasized Japan’s importance as an Australian market. He also asked about U.S. representations concerning the Yunnan Railway; Hornbeck described them and raised possible parallel British concern.

subfiles.title: Applicability of the Securities Act to Japanese bonds in the Philippines
subfiles.about: Advises that the proposed sale of Japanese government bonds in the Philippine Islands appears subject to the Securities Act.
subfiles.summary: Frank says the bonds lack an effective registration statement and that their importation for sale appears to violate the Act. He encloses the Act and regulations.

subfiles.title: Securities Act of 1933
subfiles.about: Sets out federal registration, disclosure, liability and enforcement provisions for securities, including foreign government issues.
subfiles.summary: The printed Act defines securities and interstate commerce, including commerce involving U.S. territories, and sets registration and prospectus requirements. Its exemptions do not generally cover foreign government bonds. Schedule B specifies disclosures for foreign government issues. The excerpt also covers civil liability, enforcement, and the Corporation of Foreign Security Holders; the statute continues beyond page 36.
